title: Noetherian Cohen–Macaulay rings are universally catenary
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Assume that for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subseteq R$, the local ring $R_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is Cohen–Macaulay, meaning $\operatorname{depth}(R_{\mathfrak p})=\dim(R_{\mathfrak p})$ with depth [def-weil-pbc-depth] and Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Then $R$ is universally catenary [def-exc-excellent-ring]: every finite type commutative $R$-algebra $A$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] is catenary, so between any comparable primes of $A$ finite strict prime-chain lengths have a finite upper bound and all saturated chains have the same length.

source.place: Tag 00NM, lemma-CM-ring-catenary: a Noetherian Cohen–Macaulay ring is universally catenary; the proof applies the polynomial-algebra Cohen–Macaulay result and the maximal-chain formula.

proof.text: For a finite type R-algebra A, choose a surjective algebra map f from P=R[x_1,...,x_n]. Apply [lem-trf-polynomial-algebra-cm] to obtain Noetherianity of P and depth equal to dimension at all its prime localizations.

source.place: Tag 00NM, lemma-CM-ring-catenary: a Noetherian Cohen–Macaulay ring is universally catenary; the proof applies the polynomial-algebra Cohen–Macaulay result and the maximal-chain formula.

proof.text: In the Noetherian ring P every prime has finite height (Mathlib Ideal.finiteHeight_of_isNoetherianRing). For any saturated LTSeries c from p to q choose a prefix a ending at p with length height(p), using Mathlib Ideal.exists_ltSeries_length_eq_height. The full-height formula Order.height_eq_index_of_length_eq_height_last implies that a starts at a minimal prime and its consecutive pairs are covers: an intermediate prime would increase height by at least two between consecutive indices.

source.place: Tag 00NM, lemma-CM-ring-catenary: a Noetherian Cohen–Macaulay ring is universally catenary; the proof applies the polynomial-algebra Cohen–Macaulay result and the maximal-chain formula.

proof.text: Smash a and c at p. The resulting chain b has minimal head, saturated consecutive pairs, last term q, and length height(p)+length(c). Under [lem-weil-pbc-primes-of-localization], view b as a chain bl in P_q. Its head remains minimal, its last term is maximal, and it remains saturated, hence its range is a maximal chain. Mathlib IsLocalization.AtPrime.ringKrullDim_eq_height identifies dim(P_q) with height(q); this is a natural number d because q has finite height. Local depth equals dimension, so [lem-weil-pbc-cm-local-maximal-chain-length] applied once to bl gives length(a)+length(c)=d. Therefore length(c)=height(q)-height(p). The prefix already has length height(p), so no separate application of the maximal-chain formula in P_p is needed.

source.place: Tag 00NM, lemma-CM-ring-catenary: a Noetherian Cohen–Macaulay ring is universally catenary; the proof applies the polynomial-algebra Cohen–Macaulay result and the maximal-chain formula.

proof.text: Use the order isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-homeomorphism-zero-locus] for the surjection f. Lift each finite prime chain in A to P by comap. Its length is bounded by the finite height of the lifted upper endpoint, by Order.length_le_height_last. A lifted saturated chain stays saturated: every intermediate prime contains ker(f), so the inverse order isomorphism would give an intermediate prime in A. Step 3 assigns every such chain the same difference of the lifted endpoint heights. Thus all saturated chains in each interval of A have equal natural-number lengths.

source.place: Tag 00NM, lemma-CM-ring-catenary: a Noetherian Cohen–Macaulay ring is universally catenary; the proof applies the polynomial-algebra Cohen–Macaulay result and the maximal-chain formula.

proof.text: The bounds and equal saturated-chain lengths prove IsCatenaryRing A for every finite type R-algebra A. Together with the given Noetherianity of R this is [def-exc-excellent-ring], namely IsUniversallyCatenary R. No nontriviality hypothesis was added: the zero ring has no primes, and the equal-endpoint and zero-variable cases are covered by the same argument.
